parts.label: a
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation is not mentioned anywhere in the S statements; S5.1 only covers PMCC (product moment correlation coefficient) hypothesis testing, and S2.2/S5.1 explicitly exclude calculation involving correlation coefficients via formula but do mention PMCC via calculator, not Spearman's. Spearman's rank is a named concept not covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using Spearman's rank correlation
parts.reason: Depends on Spearman's rank coefficient from part (a), which is out of spec; also no statement covers hypothesis testing with Spearman's rank (critical values table for rank correlation not mentioned).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Rationale for using rank correlation over PMCC
parts.reason: This explanation relies on understanding Spearman's rank vs PMCC, a topic not in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Concept of tied ranks in Spearman's correlation, not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests (goodness of fit) are not mentioned in any S statement; S2.4 explicitly says 'Significance tests, other than those mentioned in Section 5, will not be expected' and Section 5 only covers binomial proportion and normal mean tests, not chi-squared.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Expected frequency calculation for contingency table (chi-squared test of association)
parts.reason: Part of chi-squared test of association, not covered by any statement and excluded per S2.4.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Degrees of freedom for chi-squared test
parts.reason: Chi-squared test concept entirely absent from spec statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Two-sample z-test for difference of means
parts.reason: Hypothesis testing for difference between two population means is not covered; S5.3 only covers a test for the mean of a single Normal distribution, not two-sample tests. This is a distinct, unlisted technique.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Relies on the out-of-spec two-sample hypothesis test framework from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.reason: question dropped: other parts out of spec

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Normal distribution linear combination (sum of independent normals) is not covered by S4.2, which only covers the single Normal distribution as a model and finding probabilities, not combinations/sums of normal variables (a distinct technique not stated anywhere in the S statements).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Difference of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Same issue as (a); linear combinations of normal distributions not in spec.

parts.label: c

parts.reason: Same issue; combinations of normal random variables entirely absent from spec statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Central Limit Theorem applied to uniform distribution
parts.reason: Central Limit Theorem is explicitly excluded: S5.3 states 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations is not required.' Also uniform distribution/continuous random variable mean-variance not covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Confidence interval using CLT result for uniform distribution parameter
parts.reason: Depends on the CLT-based distribution derived in (a), which is explicitly excluded per S5.3.
